gap: No result ChatGPT got states which charger the self-heating 12V 100Ah candidates need for their heaters to turn on (for example, whether the heater runs only while a charger is connected, and at what charge current). I could not open a maker page that states it, so this is the gap still to fill, not a finding.
standout_why: I compared against TackleDirect's Dakota Lithium Powerbox 10 page (rank 2) and BiXPower's LF1220 + 60 W solar kit page (rank 5). Both already give charger rules: Dakota says it ships a 12V 3A LiFePO4 charger, should be charged at 14.4 V, and that lead-acid chargers stop at 80%. BiXPower allows only its own or authorized chargers, at most 4 batteries in series, and charging at 0–45 °C. Neither covers self-heating batteries, low-temperature cutoffs on 100Ah batteries, or a 20A charger paired with a 100Ah battery. But I could not source those facts for our candidates either, so what I can prove adds only a little to what the rivals already say.
decides: Nothing I sourced changes the pick. Rivals already state the general rule: use a 14.4–14.6 V LiFePO4 charger, because a lead-acid charger under-fills the battery. The fact that could decide between the Redodo Self-Heating and the plain low-temp-cutoff models for cold-weather buyers is whether the heater runs only from a connected charger and needs a minimum charger current. It is still unsourced and should be checked on Redodo's US product page or manual before the page says it.
